statedReasoning: Bill 24/0, led by Vít Rakušan, is titled in full 'kterým se mění zákon č. 128/2000 Sb., o obcích (obecní zřízení)... a další zákony v souvislosti s podporou spolupráce obcí' — an omnibus explicitly billed as touching 'other laws in connection with supporting municipal cooperation'. Per the full text and důvodová zpráva (read directly): the CONFIRMED substance is exactly what the census's undercount flag and prior web-search lead pointed to — expansion of the 'společenství obcí' (voluntary municipal-association) institute under §53a et seq. of zákon č. 128/2000 Sb., which currently has no public-authority powers of its own. The bill gives společenství obcí legal standing as a 'orgán veřejné moci' able to exercise delegated state-administration powers in its own name, adds its own organizational apparatus (shromáždění starostů, předseda, kancelář — an office equivalent to a municipal authority, with staff getting civil-servant/úředník status), and enables THREE concrete new optional competencies: (1) joint municipal police forces spanning member municipalities (amending zákon č. 553/1991 Sb.), (2) acting as a CzechPOINT public-administration contact point (amending zákon č. 365/2000 Sb.), and (3) jointly procuring public-transport service plans (amending zákon č. 194/2010 Sb.). It also extends public-power liability rules to společenství obcí (zákon č. 82/1998 Sb.), pay-grade parity for jejich staff (zákoník práce, č. 262/2006 Sb.), publication-registry housekeeping (zákon č. 35/2021 Sb. o Sbírce právních předpisů ÚSC), a digital-signature convenience fix (zákon č. 12/2020 Sb. o právu na digitální služby), and two largely unrelated administrative-procedure modernizations — automated decision-making and videoconferencing in správní řízení (zákon č. 500/2004 Sb., správní řád) — plus repeal of an implementing decree (vyhláška č. 553/2020 Sb. and its amendments). The DZ frames this as implementing international (OECD) and domestic (NERV) recommendations to strengthen VOLUNTARY inter-municipal cooperation as an alternative to forced municipal mergers, with membership and each specific service remaining fully opt-in for individual municipalities.
researchedContext: History confirms: submitted 12 Nov 2025, distributed 14 Nov 2025 as print 24/0, sent to government 18 Nov 2025, government returned a NEUTRAL opinion 12 Dec 2025 (print 24/1), Organizational Committee recommended proceeding 17 Dec 2025, assigning the Committee for Public Administration and Regional Development as guarantor with rapporteur Zdeňka Blišťanová (also a co-sponsor of sibling bill tisk 181). The census's large undercount finding (1 recorded vs. 10 real amended statutes) is now FULLY CONFIRMED by direct reading of the bill text, which is structured as ten numbered Parts (ČÁST PRVNÍ through JEDENÁCTÁ), each amending one of exactly the ten statutes the census identified: 128/2000 (obce, Part 1), 553/1991 (obecní policie, Part 2), 82/1998 (public-power liability, Part 3), 365/2000 (public-admin info systems / CzechPOINT, Part 4), 500/2004 (správní řád, Part 5), 262/2006 (zákoník práce, Part 6), 194/2010 (public transport services, Part 7), 12/2020 (digital services, Part 8), 35/2021 (Sbírka právních předpisů ÚSC, Part 9), plus a repeal of vyhláška č. 553/2020 Sb. and its three amending decrees (Part 10). This is a textbook conforming-amendment omnibus: the graph's title-regex extraction caught only the lead statute (128/2000) named in the bill's title line, missing the other nine parts entirely — a clean, now fully verified instance of the batch's flagged undercount pattern, worth surfacing to the graph-quality backlog exactly as originally flagged.

unstatedEffects.effect: The graph materially undercounted this bill's legislative footprint (1 recorded vs 10 real amended statutes), which is now fully confirmed by direct text reading rather than inference. Any downstream analysis (e.g. collision checks against sibling bills touching the same statutes, such as 553/1991 or 500/2004) run off the graph's amends-edges alone would have missed 9 of the 10 real touchpoints for this bill.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Not a benefit/harm finding — this is a data-quality gap affecting analytical completeness, not a policy effect.

unstatedEffects.effect: The bill gives společenství obcí (voluntary municipal associations) new public-authority status able to run joint municipal police forces and act as CzechPOINT contact points on behalf of member municipalities — a genuine institutional expansion of local self-government capacity, framed by the sponsors as OECD/NERV-recommended, entirely opt-in per municipality and per service.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: Member municipalities of existing/future společenství obcí that choose to opt into joint policing, CzechPOINT, or transit-planning services — a broad, non-targeted class of local governments, not any specific named entity.

conflictAssessment: Lead sponsors Kovářová and Rakušan (identical tied-company profile to sibling bill tisk 146) hold governance seats predominantly in state-owned or civic/NGO entities: ČEPRO, a.s. (state fuel distributor), Vodní cesty na Labi, o.p.s. (state waterways body), and several local civic associations/homeowners' bodies. Co-sponsor Lukáš Vlček holds seats at several small regional entities (SOMPO, a.s.; PEVAK Pelhřimov, družstvo — a Pelhřimov-region water cooperative; W.H.V. Projekt spol. s r.o.; Via rustica z.s.; PRO VYSOČINU; a homeowners' association). Now that the bill's actual ten-statute scope is confirmed — voluntary municipal-association powers, joint policing, CzechPOINT, transit planning, admin-procedure modernization — none of these ties connects: fuel distribution, inland waterways, a Pelhřimov water cooperative, or the small private/civic entities held by other low-tie sponsors have no plausible channel into inter-municipal-cooperation, policing, or public-administration digitalization. No plausible personal-enrichment channel identified for any sponsor's tied company against this bill's now-confirmed subject matter. Consistent with the batch's honest-absence pattern, and a stronger conclusion than the first pass given the substance is now fully verified rather than inferred from a title alone.
